## Setup {#sec-setup}

Consider an autonomous system

$$
\dot{x} = f(x), \qquad x \in \R^2,
$$ {#eq-system}

where $f$ is continuously differentiable.

::: {#def-equilibrium}
## Equilibrium

A point $x^*$ is an *equilibrium* of @eq-system if $f(x^*) = 0$. It is *asymptotically stable* if solutions that start near $x^*$ stay near it and converge to $x^*$ as $t \to \infty$, that is, $\norm{x(t) - x^*} \to 0$.
:::

Writing $x = x^* + u$ and expanding $f$ to first order gives the linearized system

$$
\dot{u} = A u, \qquad A = Df(x^*).
$$ {#eq-linear}

## Linearization {#sec-linear}

::: {#prp-linear}
The origin is an asymptotically stable equilibrium of @eq-linear if and only if every eigenvalue of $A$ has negative real part.
:::

::: {.proof}
Write $A = PJP^{-1}$ with $J$ in Jordan form, so $u(t) = P e^{Jt} P^{-1} u(0)$. Each entry of $e^{Jt}$ is a polynomial in $t$ times $e^{\lambda t}$ for an eigenvalue $\lambda$, and tends to zero exactly when $\operatorname{Re}\lambda < 0$. If some eigenvalue has $\operatorname{Re}\lambda \ge 0$, the solution along its eigenvector does not decay.
:::

::: {#thm-hartman}
## Hartman–Grobman

If no eigenvalue of $Df(x^*)$ has zero real part, then near $x^*$ the flow of @eq-system is topologically conjugate to the flow of @eq-linear [@perko2001, sec. 2.8].
:::

By @thm-hartman, a hyperbolic equilibrium of the nonlinear system has the stability that @prp-linear assigns to its linearization.[^hyperbolic]

[^hyperbolic]: An equilibrium is hyperbolic when no eigenvalue of its Jacobian lies on the imaginary axis. At non-hyperbolic points the linear terms do not decide stability [@strogatz2015, ch. 6].

## Classification {#sec-class}

For a $2 \times 2$ matrix with trace $\tau = \tr A$ and determinant $\Delta = \det A$, the eigenvalues are

$$
\lambda_{\pm} = \frac{\tau \pm \sqrt{\tau^2 - 4\Delta}}{2}.
$$ {#eq-eig}

::: {#lem-trace}
The eigenvalues satisfy $\lambda_+ + \lambda_- = \tau$ and $\lambda_+ \lambda_- = \Delta$.
:::

::: {.proof}
Both identities follow from @eq-eig, or from comparing coefficients of the characteristic polynomial $\lambda^2 - \tau\lambda + \Delta$.
:::

@tbl-class lists the cases that follow from @eq-eig and @lem-trace.

| Condition | Eigenvalues | Equilibrium |
|:----------|:------------|:------------|
| $\Delta < 0$ | real, opposite signs | saddle |
| $\tau < 0,\ \tau^2 > 4\Delta > 0$ | real, negative | stable node |
| $\tau < 0,\ \tau^2 < 4\Delta$ | complex, $\operatorname{Re}\lambda < 0$ | stable spiral |
| $\tau = 0,\ \Delta > 0$ | purely imaginary | center (linear) |
| $\tau > 0,\ \Delta > 0$ | $\operatorname{Re}\lambda > 0$ | unstable node or spiral |

: Equilibria of $\dot{u} = Au$ by trace and determinant. {#tbl-class}

::: {#exm-oscillator}
## Damped oscillator

The equation $\ddot{y} + 2\zeta \dot{y} + y = 0$ with $\zeta > 0$ becomes $\dot{u} = Au$ with

$$
A = \begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\ -1 & -2\zeta \end{pmatrix}, \qquad \tau = -2\zeta, \quad \Delta = 1.
$$

By @tbl-class the origin is a stable spiral for $0 < \zeta < 1$ and a stable node for $\zeta > 1$. @fig-phase shows a trajectory for $\zeta = 0.25$.
:::

![Phase portrait of the damped oscillator in @exm-oscillator for $\zeta = 0.25$, starting at $(1, 0)$.](phase-portrait.svg){#fig-phase fig-alt="A single trajectory that starts at the point (1, 0) and spirals clockwise into the origin, crossing the axes several times with shrinking amplitude."}

## Numerical check {#sec-code}

The script computes the eigenvalues of $A$ from @exm-oscillator and integrates the system with SciPy.

```{.python filename="stability.py"}
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp

zeta = 0.25
A = np.array([[0.0, 1.0],
              [-1.0, -2.0 * zeta]])

# Eigenvalues decide stability (Proposition 1)
print(np.linalg.eigvals(A))

sol = solve_ivp(lambda t, u: A @ u, (0, 30), [1.0, 0.0],
                max_step=0.05)
```
